request: I need a drilling template, flat, for the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 hole pattern in a panel. The Pico 2's four mounting holes are 2.1 mm and form a 47.0 x 11.4 mm rectangle (47.0 mm apart lengthwise, 11.4 mm across). Each of the four gets a 2.3 mm guide hole in the template, so a 2.1 mm drill goes through with some play. The template registers against a straight panel edge: I hold it to the edge of the panel, a flat sheet 3 mm thick, and drill. The closest row of holes has to be 10 mm from that edge; I slide it along the edge by eye, so just the distance from the edge and the angle count. In the top face there is a pocket in the shape of the Pico's outline, so I can set a Pico in it to verify placement before I drill. Hole centres have to land within 0.1 mm of the pattern. I print it in PLA on an FDM printer. Requirements: The template needs four guide holes whose axes sit on the 47.0 x 11.4 mm mounting-hole rectangle of the Pico 2, every one within 0.1 mm of where it should be, with the pattern rows parallel to the locating edge to within 0.1 degrees. The layout has to be declared. Where the pattern sits along the edge is free, so the 0.1 mm is measured after finding the best shift along that edge. All guide holes are 2.3 mm across and round to within 0.1 mm, passing through the entire plate, and they are long enough to keep a 2.1 mm drill square to the panel: 2.0 to 4.0 mm of guide length between the recess floor and the underside. The fence's flat inner face sits against the straight edge of a 3.0 mm panel while the plate lies on the panel's top face, and the nearest hole row is 10.0 mm (within 0.1 mm) from that face. The fence is no less than 2.0 mm thick and 40 mm long and extends 3.0 to 6.0 mm under the plate. On the top face there is a pocket that follows the Pico 2's outline with 0.2 mm of clearance on each side (corners rounded by 0.6 mm at most) and is 0.8 mm deep. It is centred on the hole pattern, so a Pico lying in it has its holes lined up with the guide holes. The plate is 4.0 mm thick and has a flat underside. Each hole and the pocket must have 3.0 mm or more of material between them and the plate's free edges. The template is a single manifold body that can be printed in PLA on an FDM printer, in its declared orientation, with no supports. Its size must not exceed 70 x 40 x 10 mm (X x Y x Z, closed assembly pose including the fence), and nothing may stick up above the top face of the plate. From above, a 2.1 mm drill has to be able to get to every guide hole, and the chuck needs space above the plate's top. Deliver an STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout (seating pose and print orientation) and the agent's own measurement report, which must match an independent measurement.
